recipes.name: Roasted Lamb Breast
ingredients_raw: 4 pounds lamb breast, separated in two pieces
0.5 cup chopped Italian flat leaf parsley
0.33333334326744 cup white wine vinegar, more as needed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C).
Whisk olive oil, cumin, salt, black pepper, Italian herb seasoning, cinnamon, coriander, and paprika in a large bowl until combined.
Coat lamb breasts in spice mixture, then place fat-side-up in a roasting pan. Tightly cover the roasting pan with aluminum foil.
Bake in the preheated oven until meat is tender when pierced with a fork, about 2 hours.
Meanwhile, combine chopped parsley, vinegar, fresh lemon juice, garlic, honey, red pepper flakes, and salt in a bowl. Mix well and set aside.
Increase oven temperature to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil.
Remove lamb from the roasting pan and cut into 4 pieces. Place lamb pieces on the prepared baking sheet. Brush tops with fat drippings from the roasting pan.
Roast in the preheated oven until meat is browned and edges are crispy, about 20 minutes.
Turn the oven broiler to high and brown meat until top is golden brown, about 4 minutes. Serve lamb topped with parsley-vinegar sauce.

raw_recipe.headline: Roasted Lamb Breast
raw_recipe.description: This lamb breast recipe is Chef John's method of making flavorful spice-rubbed lamb roasted until tender and served with a vinegar parsley sauce.

review.reviewBody: I decided to try this recipe after seeing lamb breast/ribs at Walmart (of all places!). It was $4 and some change for 2 rib slabs in one package. I bought 2 packages (4 ribs total) and used the measurements in this recipe. The lamb had really good flavors. Only little change I made was to cut back on the cinnamon to 1/4-1/2tsp -would have been overpowering, in my opinion, if there was more than that. I also added extra honey in the sauce and instead of broiling it in the oven, I finished it over a grill for some nice char. This cut of meat is very fatty, but delicious nonetheless.

put these on my SMOKER. wrapped them in foil, cooked 2 hours @ 240F. unwrapped, back on smoker half hour. Then placed under broiler. I also opened the fattier one and removed the excess fat before cooking , and put the rub on the day before and let them chill overnight. They were still a bit fatty, but tons of flavor and were delicious! My husband loved it! and the vinegar/parsley sauce. I also added some fresh mint to mine. SSOOO good! THANKS!

This is a winner recipe and fairly easy. I found lamb breast, a pack of two breasts, at WalMart and then this recipe. Totally delish. Here’s some hints: the rub is enough for one breast, double the rub for two. The breasts I bought were very fatty. Trim some off. After two hours at 300 degrees, the lamb is barely cooked but will cook nicely at 425. Be prepared to cook longer at 425 than the recipe calls for. I didn’t broil the breast; leaving it in the oven longer at 425 browned it nicely. Enjoy!

I picked up a 1 kg (1 lb 7 oz) pack of lamb breast for £1 in Morrisons, reduced from £10 on its expiry date. I'm so glad that I discovered this recipe, it was delicious! I didn't scale down the other ingredients but I did add a teaspoon of chilli powder for some background heat, and I marinated it overnight in a ziplock bag with a bit of extra olive oil as suggested by another reviewer. I kept the roasting timings the same, even though mine was a much smaller piece of meat. I'm not sure what an oven broiler is so I just put mine under the grill at the end, instead. I couldn't find red pepper flakes for the salsa, so I used chilli flakes. Served with flatbreads and tsatziki, it was absolutely incredible!

I am Greek and love lamb. Was in the market and saw a beautiful meaty 2.5 lb breast of lamb but since I had never cooked this cut of meat, I literally stood at the meat counter, did a web search and found this recipe.
I followed the directions for the spice rub but added 2 extra Tbs of olive oil and cut the salt to 1 tsp. I put the meat in a zip lock bag and massaged the spiced oil into the meat. I let it marinate in the fridge overnight. Cooked it as directed in a covered Corningware at 300 for 1 hour then put in on the foil covered baking tray at 450 for 30 min. It was perfect for me so I didn’t do the broiler step. I let the lamb sit and then the cut the ribs and trimmed the large chunks of fat off. It is absolutely delicious! The spices are perfect and I have enough for another meal. I will make again!

I love lamb, and like others reviewing this recipe, I ran across lamb breast at wal-mart and was intrigued. Mostly by how affordable it was. Looked up this recipe in the store, and decided to go for it. I prepped the meat as directed, but decided to slow smoke the breasts, like one would smoke ribs. Left it in the smoker for 3+ hours, then wrapped in foil for a couple more hours. The result was alot like pork belly. When all the fat was scraped away, I was left with delicious, tender, brisket textured lamb. It tasted delicious and the sauce was an excellent, bright compliment to the meat. Note that this is very fatty. 5 lbs of lamb breast yielded about 11 oz of lean meat. So I made a lamb stock for stew with all the leftover parts. I would do it again, but I will be better prepared to deal with all the rendered fat.

I prepped the lamb, season it, in the morning as I had a busy day and just wanted to be able to past by, between jobs, in the afternoon and pop it in the oven so it would be ready when we got home that evening. I also put in 1/2c water and potato’s, onions and carrots around the lamb. It was delicious, the flavour that the veggies took on was really yummy. Sadly I was so busy I forgot to do the sauce but it didn’t matter every one loved it. Mr8 thought the potato was ‘the bomb’, then again he and Miss5 love lamb :))

Our family recipe. I am 60 and MY great gran taught this to me in the 70's, so its been in the family for well over 150 years. We used to cook on a Yorkshire range. This is an open coal fire with an oven at the side. The only temp regulation was building the fire up or letting it die down OR leaving the door open. A simple one pot 3 ingredient recipe. Peel and slice into scallops enough potato to half fill the pot. Slice about 2 large onions. Layer the potato and onion in the pot. Place the breast of lamb on the top, cutting the pieces to ensure the potato is completely covered. Occasionally turn the lamb pieces to brown and crisp up both sides. You can do more than one lamb layer but you need to turn and swap it around. Low and slow is best for this. The lamb fat renders and melts through the potato/onion layers cooking them soft and mushy but with wonderful crispy edges. A HUGE amount of fat but it can be tweaked and updated by draining out a lot of the fat and adding herbs and flavoring. This was a high calorie, filling meal for the men in the family that were coal miners doing very hard labouring work. ENJOY

Very tasty but a little fatty. I would recommend trimming the fat on the ribs and also be sure to remove all sliver skin and membrane on the back of ribs. Removing silver skin will make it less gamey. I ended up cooking the ribs on the smoker with mesquite at 225 for 2 hours before quartering. Then finished on high heat on the grill for a reverse sear. The chimichurri sauce was very good too

I found the directions a bit disorganized: I skipped step 2 and went back to it after step 9. I used small bowls for steps 2 and 3, and I rubbed the olive oil into the meat, then rubbed in the rest of the step-3 spices, rather then mixing the spices with the oil before rubbing them in. Otherwise, I followed the recipe exactly. The inside meat was extremely tender and delicious, and the spices were perfect. Unfortunately, the "crispy" edge meat was dried-out and hard because it was over-done. Next time I will reduce the temperature from 450 to 425 for the 20 minute 2nd roasting, and if it still looks too well done on the outside, I will omit the final 4 minutes under the broiler. My side dishes were green beans and fennel, and oven-roasted red-skinned potato wedges. I drizzled the parsley and vinegar sauce over the veges and potatoes as well as the lamb. Delicious!
Soooo Good. Pairs well with risotto milanese and roasted carrots. Make the vinegar dressing early; it gets better with time.

Excellent, unique flavors in this recipe. I was hesitant about the sauce but trusted the process. :) We didn’t need to do the final broil - it was perfect after the higher temp roast. I’m so glad I gambled with buying this cut of meat - wasn’t sure what to do with it but half off at Aldi was too good to pass up! Will absolutely make this again.
Made this one by the book, DELICIOUS , with honey & cumin carrots.

5 for the flavor, 4 because of how fatty this cut of meat is. A boneless leg of lamb would be stellar with this recipe. Was skeptical about the flavor profile with the spice rub and parsley combo but it works! Just a touch of mint would surely kick it up more. Gonna do that on the next one. Will finish on the grill instead of broiler for a better flavor char. Great recipe for sure.

Tastes delicious, but more work than I care to do for a meal. I followed the recipe exactly. It was tedious not only preparing the dish, but cutting the lamb apart and eating it required a lot of work, too. Delicious “pesto” for on top of the meat. We served it with rice and roasted green beans. Not going to buy this cut of meat again, but might use the condiment recipe for a different grilled meat.

We bought a box of Welsh salt marsh lamb and didn't know what to do with the breast (having only had boned rolled before), so really glad we found this recipe. I didn't have pepper flakes but otherwise stuck completely to the recipe - it was tasty and juicy and worked. We also have a mutton breast from the same company and intend trying it out, though I think it will need longer cooking.
